nodes.summary: For $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, let $d = \operatorname{graph}(x \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, \operatorname{app}(x, x)))$, the denotation of $\lambda x.\, u(x\,x)$. Then the self-application of $d$ is the least fixed point of the continuous function $\operatorname{app}(u, \cdot)$: Since the paradoxical combinator $Y = \lambda u.(\lambda x.u(xx))(\lambda x.u(xx))$ sends $u$ to $\operatorname{app}(d, d)$, this says…
nodes.title: Scott's first recursion theorem in `P(ω)`

nodes.summary: Every Scott-continuous $f : P(\omega) \to P(\omega)$ is recovered from its graph: (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 1.2 (i)). Read with $\operatorname{app}$ as application and $\operatorname{graph}$ as λ-abstraction, this is the β-rule of the graph model. Together with part (ii), it makes the continuous self-maps of $P(\omega)$ a retract of $P(\omega)$.
nodes.title: Scott's graph theorem, part (i)

nodes.summary: Every set $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ acts as a function on $P(\omega)$ by (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1, definition of $\operatorname{fun}(u)(x)$; in the language LAMBDA of §2 this is the application $u(x)$).
nodes.title: Application in the graph model

nodes.summary: For every map $f : X \to P(\omega)$ on a subset $X$ of a topological space $Y$, whether continuous or not, Scott's extension $\bar f : Y \to P(\omega)$ is continuous for the Scott topology. Scott notes this explicitly: $\bar f$ is continuous "no matter what function $f$ is given" (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Appendix A, proof of Theorem 1.5). His proof shows that each set…
nodes.title: Scott's extension is continuous

nodes.summary: A map $g : Z \to P(\omega)$ from a topological space to $P(\omega)$ with its Scott topology is continuous as soon as $\{z \mid m \in g(z)\}$ is open for every $m \in \mathbb{N}$. The reason is that the Scott-open sets of $P(\omega)$ are unions of finite intersections of the sets $\{y \mid m \in y\}$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Appendix A, proof of Theorem 1.5).
nodes.title: Continuity into `P(ω)` is tested on the subbasic open sets

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a subspace of a topological space $Y$. Every continuous map $f : X \to P(\omega)$, for the Scott topology, extends to a continuous map $Y \to P(\omega)$, so $P(\omega)$ is an injective space (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Theorem 1.5). The Lean statement asserts that such an extension exists. The extension is Scott's extension $\bar f$, which is continuous and agrees…
nodes.title: Scott's extension theorem

nodes.summary: If $V$ is a Scott-open set of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and $y \in V$, then some finite subset of $y$ lies in $V$. Since Scott-open sets are upper sets, $V$ is therefore the union of the basic open sets $\{z \mid e \subseteq z\}$ over the finite $e \in V$: the open sets are the sets "of finite character" (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1).
nodes.title: Scott-open sets of `P(ω)` have finite character

nodes.summary: There is a set $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $\operatorname{graph}(x \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, x)) \ne u$. For instance $u = \{\langle n_0, 0\rangle\}$ with $e_{n_0} = \emptyset$ works: the graph of the constant function it determines also contains $\langle n_1, 0\rangle$ for $e_{n_1} = \{0\}$.
nodes.title: The graph model is not extensional

nodes.summary: Every $T_0$ space $X$ with a countable basis embeds topologically in $P(\omega)$ with its Scott topology (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Theorem 1.6). The Lean statement asserts that such an embedding exists. The proof applies Scott's embedding map $x \mapsto \{n \mid x \in U_n\}$, for an enumeration $U_0, U_1, \ldots$ of a countable family of open sets generating the topology;…
nodes.title: Scott's embedding theorem

nodes.summary: If $f : X \to P(\omega)$ is continuous on the subspace $X$ of $Y$, then Scott's extension $\bar f$ agrees with $f$ on $X$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Theorem 1.5). Scott's proof: $\bar f(x) \subseteq f(x)$ because every open $U \ni x$ contains $x$ itself. Conversely, if $m \in f(x)$, then $f^{-1}\{z \mid m \in z\}$ is open in $X$, so it is $X \cap U$ for an open $U \ni x$, and…
nodes.title: Scott's extension extends a continuous map

nodes.summary: For a subset $X$ of a topological space $Y$ and any map $f : X \to P(\omega)$, Scott's extension $\bar f : Y \to P(\omega)$ is with the empty intersection equal to $\mathbb{N}$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Theorem 1.5, the formula for the extension). Equivalently, $m \in \bar f(y)$ if and only if some open $U \ni y$ has $m \in f(x)$ for all $x \in X \cap U$.
nodes.title: Scott's extension of a map into `P(ω)`

nodes.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the finite set $e_n \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is read off the binary expansion of $n$: $k \in e_n$ if and only if the $k$-th binary digit of $n$ is $1$, so that $n = \sum_{k \in e_n} 2^k$. Every finite subset of $\mathbb{N}$ is $e_n$ for exactly one $n$, and every element of $e_n$ is smaller than $n$.
nodes.title: The `n`-th finite set of the graph model

nodes.summary: A set $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is the graph of the function it determines, $\operatorname{graph}(\operatorname{app}(u, \cdot)) = u$, exactly when $u$ is upward closed in the first coordinate: $\langle k, m\rangle \in u$ and $e_k \subseteq e_n$ imply $\langle n, m\rangle \in u$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 1.2 (iii)). Scott notes that this condition is equivalent…
nodes.title: Scott's graph theorem, part (iii)

nodes.summary: For every family $F$ of functions $P(\omega) \to P(\omega)$, the graph of the pointwise union is the union of the graphs: So $\operatorname{graph}$ is Scott-continuous, indeed completely join-preserving, for the pointwise order on functions.
nodes.title: The graph of a pointwise union

nodes.summary: For a function $f : P(\omega) \to P(\omega)$, its graph is the set of codes where $e_n$ is the $n$-th finite set and $\langle n, m\rangle$ is a pairing of natural numbers (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1, definition of $\operatorname{graph}$). Interpreted as an operation, $\operatorname{graph}$ is λ-abstraction in the graph model.
nodes.title: Graph of a function on `P(ω)`

nodes.summary: A set $s \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a compact element of the complete lattice $P(\omega)$, that is, $s \subseteq \bigcup S$ implies $s \subseteq \bigcup S_0$ for a finite $S_0 \subseteq S$, if and only if $s$ is finite. The same holds in the powerset of any type, and the Lean statement is proved in that generality. Every set is the union of its finite subsets, so $P(\omega)$ is an algebraic lattice whose compact…
nodes.title: The compact elements of `P(ω)` are the finite sets

nodes.summary: Let $X$ be a $T_0$ space whose topology is generated by open sets $U_0, U_1, \ldots$. Then the map is a topological embedding of $X$ into $P(\omega)$ with its Scott topology (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), Theorem 1.6, where the $U_n$ form a countable basis; here they need only generate the topology). The $T_0$ hypothesis makes $e$ injective. $e$ is continuous because…
nodes.title: Scott's embedding map

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the set $\{y \subseteq \mathbb{N} \mid n \in y\}$ is open in the Scott topology of $P(\omega)$. Finite intersections of these sets, $\{y \mid e \subseteq y\}$ for finite $e$, form a basis of the Scott topology (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1 and Appendix A, proof of Theorem 1.5); $P(\omega)$ is the countable power of the Sierpiński space.
nodes.title: The sets of naturals containing `n` are Scott-open

nodes.summary: If $k \in e_n$, then $k < n$: the binary digit $2^k$ occurs in $n$, so $k < 2^k \le n$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1, where Scott notes that $k \in e_n$ implies $k < n$).
nodes.title: Elements of the `n`-th finite set are smaller than `n`

nodes.summary: Let $f : P(\omega) \to P(\omega)$ be Scott-continuous, that is, preserve suprema (unions) of nonempty directed families. Then for all $x \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}$, So a continuous function is determined by its values on finite sets.
nodes.title: Scott's characterisation theorem for `P(ω)`

nodes.summary: For every $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the map $x \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, \operatorname{app}(x, x))$ is Scott-continuous. This is the function denoted by the term $\lambda x.\, u(x\,x)$, the half of the paradoxical combinator that is applied to itself.
nodes.title: Self-application is Scott-continuous

nodes.summary: For every $x \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the map $u \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, x)$ preserves all unions, in particular directed ones, so it is Scott-continuous. Scott remarks that application is even distributive in $u$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Appendix A, on equation (2.9)).
nodes.title: Application in `P(ω)` is Scott-continuous in the function

nodes.summary: For every $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the map $x \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, x)$ preserves unions of nonempty directed families, so it is Scott-continuous. In Scott's words, "every set of integers determines a continuous function" (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1, before Theorem 1.2).
nodes.title: Application in `P(ω)` is Scott-continuous in its argument

nodes.summary: The map $(u, x) \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, x)$ on $P(\omega) \times P(\omega)$ is Scott-continuous. Continuity in each variable separately implies joint continuity (D. Scott, *Continuous Lattices*, Oxford PRG-7 (1971), Proposition 2.6; D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, §1).
nodes.title: Application in `P(ω)` is jointly Scott-continuous

nodes.summary: Every set $u \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is contained in the graph of the function it determines: $u \subseteq \operatorname{graph}(x \mapsto \operatorname{app}(u, x))$ (D. Scott, *Data types as lattices*, SIAM J. Comput. 5(3) (1976), 522–587, Theorem 1.2 (ii)). Scott's proof takes, for $\langle n, m\rangle \in u$, the finite set $e_n$ itself as the witness.
nodes.title: Scott's graph theorem, part (ii)

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
